title: Church, religion and his daughters' singing
summary: He is Catholic, his daughter is a nun with a three-octave range, and his younger daughter sings in a trio.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Did I ask you about any music you heard in church? No you didn't. Did your church have any training? Did you sing in church? No I never did.
Your children did. What religion are you?

A Catholic. In fact I have a, my daughter is a nun, my oldest daughter. She sings in a choir now. And she has a very flexible voice of about three octaves, which is quite phenomenal I think. She sings soprano and turns right around and sings the alto part, either one.
That's funny. She must really have a voice to do that.
She has a very, very long extended range, three octaves.
It seems to me people are getting more training in music now. Yeah.

Through the schools and the religion, the church. We lived over in Slidell for quite a while you know, and we used to attend services at the little church there, and the priest used to always thank my little girl for being in the choir because sometimes she was the only one up there to sing you know. And both of them used to go up there and sing. In fact the younger one now is practicing with a trio, two other girls and herself, you know, and then we had to wake up some stuff. Of course on the rock and roll side, but.
Well the Bonneville sisters did well in their day here with that same type of setup. Yeah.
